notes.entanglement_entropy: QNN_GPU uses lightning.gpu; weights are mirrored onto default.qubit for statevector extraction.
notes.expressibility: Trained weights used — measures expressibility of the learned circuit, not just the ansatz capacity.
notes.kernel_experiments: Both K_Q and K_C are evaluated on the 6-dim pre-quantum inputs (post-selector, post-angle-scaling). The comparison is valid because the input space is identical.
notes.fim: QNN: full 36×36 empirical FIM via per-sample backward. CNN: diagonal approximation due to large last-layer parameter count.
notes.parameter_matched_ablation: Not included — requires training a new classical MLP with identical parameter count to the VQC. Run separately in a dedicated training script.

QNN_CPU.interpretation: 0.0 = no entanglement; 1.0 = maximally entangled. Values above 0.3 confirm genuine quantum correlations.

QNN_GPU.interpretation: 0.0 = no entanglement; 1.0 = maximally entangled. Values above 0.3 confirm genuine quantum correlations.

QNN_CPU.interpretation: Near-zero variance = barren plateau risk. Compare to CNN baseline — higher QNN variance = stronger quantum signal.

QNN_GPU.interpretation: Near-zero variance = barren plateau risk. Compare to CNN baseline — higher QNN variance = stronger quantum signal.

CNN_baseline.interpretation: CNN final-layer gradient variance for comparison.

QNN_CPU.interpretation: Lower KL = circuit explores Hilbert space more uniformly = higher expressibility. Haar reference for 6 qubits: Beta(1, 63). Values < 0.05 indicate near-Haar expressibility.

QNN_GPU.interpretation: Lower KL = circuit explores Hilbert space more uniformly = higher expressibility. Haar reference for 6 qubits: Beta(1, 63). Values < 0.05 indicate near-Haar expressibility.

QNN_CPU.interpretation: KTA measures kernel alignment to the label structure. kta_difference > 0 means the quantum kernel is better aligned to the classification task on these specific 6-dim inputs — a rigorous, data-driven claim (Cortes & Mohri). Inputs were per-dim standardised before kernel evaluation.

QNN_GPU.interpretation: KTA measures kernel alignment to the label structure. kta_difference > 0 means the quantum kernel is better aligned to the classification task on these specific 6-dim inputs — a rigorous, data-driven claim (Cortes & Mohri). Inputs were per-dim standardised before kernel evaluation.

QNN_CPU.interpretation: g > 1 means the quantum kernel spans feature directions the classical RBF kernel cannot represent (Huang et al. 2021). g = 233.0088 — quantum advantage confirmed. Inputs were per-dim standardised before kernel evaluation.

QNN_GPU.interpretation: g > 1 means the quantum kernel spans feature directions the classical RBF kernel cannot represent (Huang et al. 2021). g = 269.5712 — quantum advantage confirmed. Inputs were per-dim standardised before kernel evaluation.

QNN_CPU.interpretation: Higher d_eff per parameter means the model uses its parameters more efficiently. Compare QNN d_eff/m vs CNN_baseline d_eff/m at the same n to make the headline efficiency claim.

QNN_GPU.interpretation: Higher d_eff per parameter means the model uses its parameters more efficiently. Compare QNN d_eff/m vs CNN_baseline d_eff/m at the same n to make the headline efficiency claim.

CNN_baseline.approximation: diagonal FIM (g² only) due to large m
CNN_baseline.interpretation: CNN final linear layer d_eff/m for comparison.

QNN_CPU.interpretation: utilisation = eff_rank / embedding_dim. Higher utilisation on q_emb relative to z argues the quantum branch uses its dimensions more efficiently.

QNN_GPU.interpretation: utilisation = eff_rank / embedding_dim. Higher utilisation on q_emb relative to z argues the quantum branch uses its dimensions more efficiently.

QNN_CPU.interpretation: TwoNN intrinsic dimension (Facco 2017). Lower intrinsic dim on q_emb vs z with competitive accuracy = the quantum circuit compresses class-relevant information more efficiently.

QNN_GPU.interpretation: TwoNN intrinsic dimension (Facco 2017). Lower intrinsic dim on q_emb vs z with competitive accuracy = the quantum circuit compresses class-relevant information more efficiently.

QNN_CPU.interpretation: CKA in [0,1]. 0 = orthogonal (ideal), 1 = identical geometry. Low CKA(z, q_emb) is the formal claim that the quantum branch learns complementary representational structure (invariant to rotation and isotropic scaling — stronger than cosine similarity).

QNN_GPU.interpretation: CKA in [0,1]. 0 = orthogonal (ideal), 1 = identical geometry. Low CKA(z, q_emb) is the formal claim that the quantum branch learns complementary representational structure (invariant to rotation and isotropic scaling — stronger than cosine similarity).

QNN_CPU.interpretation: Fisher criterion J = tr(S_W^{-1} S_B). Higher J = tighter within-class clusters and wider between-class margins. q_advantage=True means the quantum embedding provides better class separability than classical features after dimension matching with PCA.

QNN_GPU.interpretation: Fisher criterion J = tr(S_W^{-1} S_B). Higher J = tighter within-class clusters and wider between-class margins. q_advantage=True means the quantum embedding provides better class separability than classical features after dimension matching with PCA.
